question: What becomes the major driving force in the movement of water in the xylem during the day?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Transpiration pull**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Transpiration pull** is the major driving force for the movement of water through the xylem during the day.
 
• It occurs due to the evaporation of water from the surface of leaves, creating a negative pressure or suction force in the xylem vessels.
 
• This negative pressure helps in pulling water upward from the roots to the leaves, overcoming gravity.
 
• The cohesive and adhesive properties of water molecules play a crucial role in maintaining the continuous column of water in the xylem.
 
• **Transpiration pull** is most effective during the day due to higher rates of transpiration under sunlight and warmer temperatures.
